title: Descent to a finite coefficient field; $\Dctf(X,\Qlb)$ as a $2$-colimit
statement:
The coefficient ring $\Qlb$ is a filtered union of the fields $E$, but integral lattices exist
only over a single $E$. We therefore show that every object and every morphism of
$\Dbc(X,\Qlb)$ is defined over some finite $E$. For $C\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},E)$ and a finite
extension $F/E$ we write $C_F=F_X\otimes_{E_X}C$ and $C_{\Qlb}=\QbarX\otimes_{E_X}C$ for the
extensions of scalars, given by functors $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},E)\to D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},F)$ and
$D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},E)\to D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Qlb)$; since $F_X$ and $\QbarX$ are flat over
$E_X$ ([lem-sfb-subfield-flat], [lem-sfb-qlbar-flat]), these need no deriving.

Let $X$ be a standing scheme.

1. Every lisse $\QbarX$-module is isomorphic to $L_{\Qlb}$ for a lisse $E_X$-module $L$ and
   some finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$.
2. For $C,D\in\Dbc(X,E)$ and every integer $r$, extension of scalars induces an isomorphism
   $$
   \varinjlim_{F\supset E}\Hom_{D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},F)}(C_F,D_F[r])\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
   \Hom_{D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Qlb)}(C_{\Qlb},D_{\Qlb}[r]),
   $$
   the colimit running over finite extensions $F$ of $E$ in $\Qlb$.
3. Every object of $\Dbc(X,\Qlb)$ is isomorphic to $K_{\Qlb}$ for some $K\in\Dbc(X,E)$ and
   some finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$.

4. For rational coefficients $\Dctf=\Dbc$; these are the bounded constructible categories
   $D_{\mathrm{cons}}$ of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. By (2) with $r=0$ and (3), extension
   of scalars identifies
   $$
   \Dctf(X,\Qlb)\simeq\mathop{\text{2-colim}}_{E\subset\Qlb}\Dctf(X,E)
   $$
   as ordinary categories (in the sense of [sk-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit]): every object of
   $\Dctf(X,\Qlb)$ is isomorphic to $K_{\Qlb}$ for some finite $E$ and some $K\in\Dctf(X,E)$, and
   for $K,L\in\Dctf(X,E)$ extension of scalars induces a bijection
   $$
   \varinjlim_{F\supset E}\Hom_{\Dctf(X,F)}(K_F,L_F)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Hom_{\Dctf(X,\Qlb)}(K_{\Qlb},L_{\Qlb}),
   $$
   the colimit running over finite extensions $F$ of $E$ in $\Qlb$.

proof.text: Finite type over Spec k makes X locally Noetherian, and quasi-compactness makes it compact. Assemble IsNoetherian X and obtain the characteristic-prime instance from hp and CharP.char_is_prime_or_zero.

Compare the two constructibility predicates on every Noetherian stratum. Finite constant models imply local finite presentation by HasFiniteConstantLocalModel.isLocallyFinitelyPresented. Conversely the finite-field and algebraic-closure local-triviality theorems, reused through finite_lf and algcl_lf, give local finite free presentations. A finite free module is pulled back from the same finite free condensed module on the point. Pullback preserves finite sums and the regular module. Transport the local finite-presentation and free-module conditions through the invertible canonical coefficient comparison. Use the same finite stratification, and then apply this equivalence to each cohomology sheaf, retaining the identical boundedness condition. This proves constantModelBoundedConstructible = boundedConstructible for both rational coefficients. Empty schemes, empty strata and rank zero use the same constructions.
Apply coefficient_finite_descent_lisse on the resulting qcqs scheme and take its first clause. This gives assertion (1) with exactly the original scalar extension.

For the Hom assertion regard C and D[r] as ambient bounded constructible objects via the predicate equality and the triangulatedness supplied by finiteBoundedTriangulated. Apply the last two representative clauses of coefficient_finite_descent_hom at degree zero. The zero-shift natural isomorphism turns its representatives into morphisms with unshifted target T(D[r]); composition with its inverse gives the reverse conversion. The specified finite comparisons agree: extendScalarsIsoOfEq commutes with inverse, and mapDerivedCategoryNatIso commutes with inverse, so finiteDescentDerivedComp is the inverse of condensedCoefficientCompIso. Thus coefficientDescentHomTransition at zero is exactly finiteDescentDerivedHomTransition, and the algebraic-closure evaluation is exactly finiteDescentDerivedHomToAlgCl. Transport surjectivity and eventual equality through these zero-shift identifications.
Take the first clause of coefficient_finite_descent_objects. It already uses the same constant-model bounded constructible objects and the same derived extensions, giving assertion (3).

For each finite field and for the algebraic closure, apply localizingClosure_ctf_equals_bc to its identity coefficient isomorphism. Its first assertion, third clause gives constantModelBoundedConstructible intersect finiteTorAmplitude = constantModelBoundedConstructible. Pair these with the predicate equalities proved above.

Use the existing constructibleCocone_isFilteredTwoColimit theorem on the Noetherian underlying space. It concerns exactly the cocone in the unchanged conclusion. Its proof assembles the existing object, Hom-surjectivity and Hom-injectivity clauses, so the explicit cocone construction and its coherence need not be reconstructed here.
